subject: javascript
summary: Explains JavaScript variable declarations (var/let/const), scoping rules, hoisting, and implicit type coercion for reading and debugging code.
key_points: var has function scope; let and const have block scope.
Hoisting moves declarations up but var initializes as undefined while let throws ReferenceError (TDZ).
Implicit type coercion causes unexpected results — prefer explicit conversions and ===.
misconceptions: var and let can always be used interchangeably.
const prevents any modification to the assigned value including object properties.
== and === behave the same way for all comparisons.
check_questions: What is the difference between var, let, and const scoping?
Why does a setTimeout loop with var print the same value?
When should === be used instead of ==?

practical_judgment_candidates: Deciding whether var-to-let replacement is safe
scenario_candidates: setTimeout loop output prediction with var vs let

common_wrong_answer_patterns: Confusing hoisting behavior of var and let
